questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
questions.worked_solution:
Using the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta ,$ we rewrite and simplify the expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we operate the first two terms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{cot}^{2}⁡x}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}-1+{sin}^{2}⁡x & =\frac{({cot}^{2}⁡x-{csc}^{2}⁡x)}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}+{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{-({csc}^{2}⁡x-{cot}^{2}⁡x)}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}+{sin}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the identity ${csc}^{2}⁡x-{cot}^{2}⁡x=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-({csc}^{2}⁡x-{cot}^{2}⁡x)}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}+{sin}^{2}⁡x & =\frac{-1}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}+{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =-{sin}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1} & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot {tan}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }} \\  & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we multiply the numerator and the denominator of our expression by $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1.$ This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)}{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the identity ${csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1={cot}^{2}⁡\theta $, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)}{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)}{{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\cancel{\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }\,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)}{\cancel{\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1) \\  & =\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }}\,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }}+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =1+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we put both fractions over a common denominator and then subtract, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1}-\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1} & =\frac{1\cdot (\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)}{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)}-\frac{1\cdot (\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)}{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)-(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)}{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1}{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1} \\  & =\frac{2}{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the identity ${csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1={cot}^{2}⁡\theta ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1} & =\frac{2}{{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =2{tan}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1}-\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1}=2{tan}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

questions.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $({cot}^{2}⁡x+1)^{2}-2{csc}^{2}⁡x+1?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we recall the identities

$$
{cot}^{2}⁡x+1={csc}^{2}⁡x,\,{csc}^{2}⁡x-1={cot}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Then, we simplify our expression using the above identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}({cot}^{2}⁡x+1)^{2}-2{csc}^{2}⁡x+1 & =({csc}^{2}⁡x)^{2}-2\cdot {csc}^{2}⁡x\cdot 1+{1}^{2} \\  & =({csc}^{2}⁡x-1)^{2} \\  & =({cot}^{2}⁡x)^{2} \\  & ={cot}^{4}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  & =\frac{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )\,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}\,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}{\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }}-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  \\  & =\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }+\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta -\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}

First, using the identity $1 + \cot^2 \theta = \csc^2 \theta,$ we rewrite the expression in the parentheses: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,(1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta )=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot {csc}^{2}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the fact that $\csc {\theta} = \dfrac{1}{\sin{\theta}},$ we can further simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot {csc}^{2}⁡\theta  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$
